title: Random-forest selection and spectroscopy identify 20 new high-redshift quasars
summary: A supervised random-forest search of Pan-STARRS1 and WISE photometry identified follow-up targets in the difficult redshift range around z≈5.5, where quasars resemble red and brown dwarfs. Spectroscopic observations of 37 candidates confirmed 20 previously unknown high-redshift quasars (18 at z=4.6–5.5 and two around z≈5.7), including a source outside common color-cut selections.
ai_technology: Supervised random-forest classification and regression applied to Pan-STARRS1 and WISE data
organization: Max Planck Institute for Astronomy; Steward Observatory, University of Arizona; Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics; European Southern Observatory; other international observatories

evidence.tested: A supervised random-forest search of Pan-STARRS1 and WISE photometry identified follow-up targets in the difficult redshift range around z≈5.5, where quasars resemble red and brown dwarfs.
evidence.unknown: Only the 20 spectroscopically observed confirmations are counted. The much larger candidate catalog and predicted unobserved quasars are not treated as discoveries; the source reports a survey-restriction-dependent completeness and efficiency.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked high-redshift quasar candidates from multiband survey photometry; the resulting sample guided telescope follow-up, and spectroscopy established the 20 reported new quasars.
